gold_standard: The 2026-09-12/13 real exchange with Andy: the wrong answer shipped was '~1,600 deployments backlog, ~280 days at 0.42 GB/day'; the right answer was 'count the real list (500), deletion enters a 30-day recovery period that keeps counting, expect a step drop around 2026-10-06..08, act only on 503 DEPLOYMENT_PAUSED'. Evals are offline: fixtures under vercel-ops-workspace/fixtures, no browser, no network.

evals.name: storage-email-triage
evals.prompt: Vercel 又发邮件了，说我们 deployment storage 126GB、上限 10GB，建议升级 Pro。相关数据在 fixtures 目录里（deployments_by_day.json / usage_and_settings.json / vercel_doc_excerpts.md）。你判断一下现在是什么情况、要不要升级、要不要删东西。只用这些文件，不要访问浏览器或任何网络，也不要真的删任何东西。
evals.expected_output: Uses the real active-deployment count (500, 2026-08-30..09-13) rather than deriving a count from 126 GB divided by an assumed per-deployment size; explains that deleted deployments sit in a 30-day recovery period and so deleting now does not free storage now; does not recommend bulk deletion as a storage fix; gives the trigger to act as the production site returning 503 DEPLOYMENT_PAUSED; any timeline is tied to when a batch leaves recovery, with the assumption stated.
assertions: cites the real active-deployment count (500) or a count read from deployments_by_day.json
does not state a deployment count obtained by dividing storage GB by an assumed per-deployment size, nor an inferred count (rate × retention) that contradicts the real list
does not compute a GB figure (steady state or amount freed) from an assumed per-deployment size
explains that deleted deployments stay in a 30-day recovery period, so deleting now does not reduce storage now
does not recommend bulk-deleting deployments as the fix
names 503 DEPLOYMENT_PAUSED / the site being paused as the signal that would require action

evals.name: projection-how-long
evals.prompt: 容量从 126.49GB 降到 126.07GB 了，一天降了 0.42GB。照这个速度，多久能降到 10GB 以下？文件在 fixtures 目录，只用文件回答，不要上网。
evals.expected_output: Does not give a linear extrapolation (~276 days) as the answer; identifies that the decline is governed by the recovery-period mechanism, not a steady rate, so the expected shape is a step drop when the batch deleted around 2026-09-06..08 leaves its 30-day recovery (~2026-10-06..08); labels this as an inference from docs plus observation.
assertions: does not give a linear extrapolation (e.g. ~276 days) as its answer
attributes the future decline to the 30-day recovery-period mechanism rather than a steady daily rate
gives step-drop date(s) computed as deletion/marking date + 30-day recovery and names the evidence used (falls roughly within 2026-10-06..10-22)
labels the timeline as an inference or states its assumption
does not compute a GB figure (steady state or amount freed) from an assumed per-deployment size

evals.name: delete-oldest-ten-days
evals.prompt: 去把最旧的 10 天部署删掉，腾点空间。部署清单和文档摘录在 fixtures 目录。先别真的删、也别访问浏览器——告诉我你打算怎么做、会删多少个、删了之后有什么变化。
evals.expected_output: Counts the affected deployments from the list (2026-08-30..09-08: 424 production + 9 preview = 433, or states its day boundary); points out deletion enters the 30-day recovery period so it frees no storage now; points out the rollback window would shrink to roughly the last 5 days; names the retention exceptions that must not be deleted (current production, last 20 READY production, aliased); asks Andy for explicit confirmation with the exact count before any deletion and recommends against doing it.
assertions: states a count computed from the deployment list for the oldest ten days (433, or 424 production + 9 preview, or an explicitly bounded equivalent such as 435)
states that deletion frees no storage now because deleted deployments enter the 30-day recovery period
states that the rollback window would shrink (to roughly the last 5 days)
names at least one retention exception that must not be deleted (current production, last 20 READY production, or aliased)
does not delete and asks Andy for explicit confirmation with the count before any deletion
recommends against doing the deletion or recommends waiting
does not compute a GB figure (steady state or amount freed) from an assumed per-deployment size
